title: Inadvertent Context Leakage in Language Models
abstract: arXiv:2608.19857v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: For AI agents to be useful beyond simple chat, they must hold sensitive user context such as calendars, credentials, health records, and financial data. We study whether the mere presence of such secrets in a model's context window introduces hidden correlations into the model's benign outputs, allowing reconstruction even when the model correctly refuses direct extraction. We further study whether an adversary can actively engineer prompts that amplify this effect, using the model as a covert carrier to transmit secrets through seemingly innocuous text. In both cases, this limited leakage is exploited using a novel adaptive attack that assumes black-box access to the underlying model. translated_title: 语言模型中的无意上下文泄露
translated_abstract: arXiv:2608.19857v1 公告类型：新 摘要：为了让AI代理在简单聊天之外更有用，它们必须持有敏感的用户上下文，如日历、凭证、健康记录和财务数据。我们研究的是，这类秘密仅仅出现在模型的上下文窗口中，是否会在模型的无害输出中引入隐藏相关性，使得即使模型正确拒绝直接提取，也能重建这些秘密。我们进一步研究，对手是否能主动设计提示词来放大这种效应，利用模型作为隐蔽载体，通过看似无害的文本传输秘密。在这两种情况下，这种有限的泄露都通过一种新颖的自适应攻击被利用，该攻击假设对底层模型具有黑盒访问权限。在对八个专有模型进行的受控实验中，我们发现，2位数的上下文秘密能以近乎完美的准确率被重建，4位数秘密的精确匹配率达到82%，所有这些都来自模型对普通、非对抗性提示产生的输出。
tldr: 本文发现语言模型在上下文窗口中持有敏感秘密时，其普通输出会隐藏泄露这些秘密的相关性，并提出了黑盒自适应攻击方法，在八个专有模型上实现了高精度的秘密重建。
en_tdlr: This paper reveals that language models leak in-context secrets through benign outputs due to hidden correlations, and proposes a black-box adaptive attack achieving near-perfect reconstruction of 2-digit and 82% exact match for 4-digit secrets across eight proprietary models.
